**EatPoint 0.3.1**, a fork of [OpenNutriTracker](https://github.com/simonoppowa/OpenNutriTracker) that counts food in points: 1 point is 100 kcal of carbohydrate, protein or fat.

> **Preview build.** Installs as its own app (`io.github.grohle.eatpoint`), not on Google Play or the App Store yet. It updates 0.3.0 and earlier EatPoint builds in place, keeping your data.

## What's new in 0.3.1

**Google Drive for the shared household**
- The household can now sync through a folder in your Google Drive (it was marked "in development" in 0.3.0).
- Whoever creates the household signs in with Google; EatPoint creates a **Hogar EatPoint** folder and shares it with the other members' Google accounts. The others scan the invite QR and sign in with their own account.
- Everything is encrypted on the phone before it is uploaded: Drive only stores unreadable `.json.enc` files.
- If Google asks you to sign in again, use **Reconnect Google** on the household screen.
- Google requires a one-time setup in Google Cloud (about 10 minutes): see the [Google Drive guide](https://github.com/Grohle/EatPoint/blob/main/docs/google-drive.md).

## Everything from 0.3.0
Food database to download, French, German and Italian, complete Spanish, diet profile with allergies and intolerances, menu generator, weekly suggestions, fibre points, household portions, meal completion, muscle goals and the searchable dish picker. See the [0.3.0 notes](https://github.com/Grohle/EatPoint/releases/tag/v0.3.0).

## Coming next
- More languages, with label and menu reading in each.
- On-device AI model for labels and menus.

## Downloads
- `EatPoint-0.3.1-arm64-v8a.apk`: for almost every phone from the last few years.
- `EatPoint-0.3.1-armeabi-v7a.apk`: for older 32-bit phones (Android 8.0+).
